newsitem.title: USA: Witness in Shakur case shot in New Jersey.
newsitem.headline: Witness in Shakur case shot in New Jersey.

text.p: A witness in the fatal shooting of Tupac Shakur has been killed in New Jersey, but his slaying did not appear at this point to be related to the rapper's death, police said.
Police responding to a report early on Sunday morning that a young man had been shot found Yafeu Fula, 19, in a low-income housing project in Orange, New Jersey. He had been shot once in the head.
Fula was taken to a nearby hospital and placed on a life support system, but was pronounced dead several hours later.
Two suspects, both juveniles, were arrested in the case and were expected to face homicide and other charges, police said on Thursday.
"As far as we know, at this time, there is no connection" to the Shakur homicide, said Orange Police Capt. Richard Contee.

Fula, of East Orange, New Jersey, was in a car in Shakur's entourage when the rap star was shot on Sept. 7 in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas. Shakur, 25, was shot after leaving a heavyweight fight between Mike Tyson and Bruce Seldon and died six days later.

Fula spoke to Las Vegas police after the shooting but later, like other members of Shakur's entourage, hired a lawyer and then refused to talk to authorities, police said. Las Vegas police have voiced frustration with the lack of cooperation among witnesses in the case.
Fula was a member of Outlaw Immortalz, a rap group that toured with Shakur under the name Thug Life and also appeared on Shakur's album "All Eyez on Me."
